task_instance: Create a new GitHub Agentic Workflow (a weekly 'stale issue digest' workflow) as .github/workflows/stale-issue-digest.md in a sample repo, following the gh-aw create-agentic-workflow.md prompt referenced by the skill's router, then compile it with the gh aw CLI into a valid .lock.yml GitHub Actions workflow and lint it.
evidence: 1) Read skill router SKILL.md at /home/user/skill-achievability-compiler/benchmark/ce_sources/cli__cli__agentic-workflows/SKILL.md; it dispatches to files under github/gh-aw's .github/aw/ directory (not local). 2) Fetched create-agentic-workflow.md, syntax*.md, triggers.md from raw.githubusercontent.com/githubnext/gh-aw (network reachable) into ./aw/. 3) The gh CLI (v2.45.0) was already present on the system; cloned githubnext/gh-aw source via `add_repo` + `git clone --depth 1` (read access granted automatically as a public repo) to ./gh-aw-src. 4) Built the CLI from source: `go build -o gh-aw-bin ./cmd/gh-aw` in gh-aw-src succeeded (Go 1.26.8 present), producing a 52MB working binary (`gh-aw-bin --version` -> 'gh aw version dev'). 5) Created sample git repo at ./sample-repo with .github/workflows/stale-issue-digest.md following the skeleton/checklist in create-agentic-workflow.md (schedule + workflow_dispatch trigger, read-only permissions, gh-proxy github tool, create-issue safe-output, noop guidance). 6) Ran `gh-aw-bin compile stale-issue-digest` inside sample-repo -> '✓ .github/workflows/stale-issue-digest.md (118.6 KB)' producing stale-issue-digest.lock.yml (121KB). 7) Verified the generated file is valid YAML with python3 yaml.safe_load (top-level keys: name, on(True), permissions, concurrency, run-name, env, jobs). 8) Ran `gh-aw-bin lint` (bundled actionlint 1.7.12) on the .lock.yml -> 'Checked 1 workflow(s), No issues found'. This confirms the skill's core deliverable (design/create/compile an agentic workflow into a valid GitHub Actions workflow file) is fully achievable in this runtime without any credentials, GitHub auth, or account-bound services -- gh auth was not needed since compile/lint operate purely on local files.
